# Workflows

## `ci.yml`: every pull request, every push to `main`, nightly and the "Run workflow" button

The nightly (04:37 UTC) tests the integration branch (`NIGHTLY_BRANCH`, `spec/33-broadside-v1`); GitHub runs schedules from `main`'s copy of the file, so it starts once this file is on `main`. Pushes, the nightly, the button and pull requests into `main` or from a `release/*` branch run everything below on every OS; other pull requests run what their change can affect ([below](#what-a-pull-request-skips)).

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | ubuntu | Decides whether the run is full or narrowed and which jobs run (`.github/scripts/ci-plan.sh`, tested first by `.github/scripts/test-ci-plan.sh`), and writes the plan, with the affected projects, to the job summary. On a pull request it installs `dotnet-affected` 7.0.1 and runs it over every project of the repository (samples outside the solution included) against the merge commit's first parent. |
| `build-test` | ubuntu, windows, macos | Full: `dotnet build Broadside.slnx -c Release -warnaserror`, then `dotnet test Broadside.Core.slnf` with TRX reports uploaded as `test-results-<os>`. On Linux and Windows the CoreGraphics and Android backends drop out through the `BroadsideBuildPlatformBackends` gate; macOS installs the `macos ios maccatalyst android` workloads first and builds them (the CoreGraphics package for macOS, iOS and Mac Catalyst), then also runs `tests/Broadside.Rendering.CoreGraphics.Tests`, the CoreGraphics backend's golden-image and allocation tests (issue #125). Windows also runs `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Direct2D.Tests` (Direct2D on a WARP device against the golden images, outside the solution filter because it needs Windows) and `tests/Broadside.Viewer.Wpf.Tests` (the WPF viewer: controller, control and automation peers, and the UI Automation test that drives `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Wpf.Sample` over the pinned subset, #222), and dry-runs `bench/Broadside.Rendering.Direct2D.Benchmarks`. Linux also runs the guide samples (`samples/guides/run-samples.sh`: every console sample whose code the site's guides include, #267), reruns the `SimdKernel` test category with `DOTNET_EnableHWIntrinsic=0` (the scalar fallback of every SIMD kernel, #470; seconds, on the same build), packs the core packages, checks them with `tools/PackageCheck` (dependency allowlists, symbols, SourceLink, licences, README and icon; offline) and uploads them as `packages`. Narrowed: each OS builds the affected projects of its set (written into `artifacts/ci/build.slnf`); a leg with none reports success at once. Linux builds the affected projects of `Broadside.Core.slnf` and of the few projects nothing else builds (the builder samples, `SampleTimings`, the sample-document generator, `BenchGate`, `ConformanceCheck`, `CorpusFetcher`, `DocSnippets`), runs their tests and the `SimdKernel` rerun without the `Category=Exhaustive` sweeps (their samples run instead), runs the builder samples and the guide samples if affected, and does not pack. Windows builds the affected Direct2D backend, tests and benchmarks, the WPF viewer, its tests and sample, and `Broadside.Rendering.Tests`, and runs the Direct2D, WPF and `Category=RenderHash` tests and the Direct2D dry run of those. macOS likewise for the CoreGraphics backend, its tests and benchmarks, the Android backend and its device and host test projects (the workloads are installed only if one of those is affected), and the render-hash test. |
| `aot-smoke` | ubuntu, windows, macos | `dotnet publish tests/Broadside.Rendering.AotSmoke -c Release --use-current-runtime` (Native AOT, trimmed, trim and AOT warnings are errors), then runs the executable with `--require-aot`: it renders the rendering corpus files with the software rasterizer, compares every pixel with the reviewed snapshots of `Broadside.Rendering.Tests`, round-trips the PNG output (issue #95), and extracts the text of a corpus file, saves it and opens it again (issue #272). |
| `size-probes` | macos, ubuntu, windows | `bench/size-probes.sh`: publishes the Native AOT size probes of `bench/SizeProbes` (one tiny app per scenario: empty, open and read metadata, extract text, render, fill a form, save, sign), runs each over a corpus file, then `BenchGate sizes` compares their sizes with the runner's runtime identifier in `bench/baselines/gate/sizes.json` (`osx-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `win-x64`, issue #272) and fails on growth past 1%, a new probe or a missing one (issue #361, `bench/baselines/gate/README.md`, "Size probes"). |
| `verapdf` | ubuntu | Installs veraPDF 1.28.2 (pinned, SHA-256 checked, headless IzPack install, Temurin 21) and runs the `Category=VeraPdf` tests of `tests/Broadside.Tests` and `tests/Broadside.Fonts.Standard14.Tests` with `BROADSIDE_REQUIRE_VERAPDF=1`: documents saved as PDF/A-2b must pass veraPDF's PDF/A-2B profile with no failed rule (#201). Locally those tests skip when `verapdf` is not on the PATH (or at `BROADSIDE_VERAPDF`). |
| `api-surface` | ubuntu (PRs only) | Writes the diff of every `src/**/PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` and `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` against the base branch to the job summary. Never fails; the PublicApiAnalyzers already fail the build on an undeclared API change. |
| `conformance-map` | ubuntu | Builds the packages whose clause citations are checked (`Broadside`, `Broadside.Fonts.Cmaps`, `Broadside.Fonts.Standard14`, `Broadside.Layout`, `Broadside.Rendering`), then `dotnet run --project tools/ConformanceCheck -- --root . --summary --citations` into the job summary. Fails on a malformed row, a `done` row without a test, a public type of a checked package that cites no specification and is not exempt in `docs/conformance/citation-policy.json`, or a row whose implementing type does not cite the row's clause (issues #7, #240). |
| `format` | ubuntu | `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` on `Broadside.Core.slnf`, `tests/Broadside.Fuzz`, `bench/Broadside.Benchmarks`, `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Direct2D.Tests`, `bench/Broadside.Rendering.Direct2D.Benchmarks`, `tests/Broadside.Viewer.Wpf.Tests` and `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Wpf.Sample` (the last six are outside the solution filter). |
| `fuzz-build` | ubuntu | Builds `tests/Broadside.Fuzz` once, `--list`s its targets and gives each a time: 60 s on full runs; on a narrowed pull request 60 s to the targets whose code changed (`tests/Broadside.Fuzz/smoke-areas.txt`, one expression of changed paths per target; any change under `tests/Broadside.Fuzz/` counts for every target) and 15 s to the rest. Uploads the build and the plan as `fuzz-harness` (kept one day). |
| `fuzz-smoke (<shard>/6)` | ubuntu | Six parallel shards: each downloads `fuzz-harness` onto a checkout and runs `--smoke <target> <seconds>` for every target whose index modulo 6 is its shard; uploads `artifacts/fuzz/**` as `fuzz-findings-<shard>` on failure. Reports success without doing anything when `fuzz-build` did not run. |
| `bench-dry` | ubuntu | `dotnet run --project bench/Broadside.Benchmarks -- --filter '*' --job dry`: one iteration of every benchmark, no measurement; then the same for the realistic tier, `bench/Broadside.Benchmarks.Realistic` (the sample documents, not gated, #363). |
| `blazor-wasm / blazor-wasm (chrome <browsers>)` | ubuntu | Calls [`blazor-wasm.yml`](#blazor-wasmyml-the-blazor-webassembly-sample-in-browsers) with `browsers: firefox` on pull requests into the integration branch, and `firefox webkit` on pull requests into `main` and pushes to `main` (#389). |
| `maui` | macOS | Installs the `maui` workload and builds `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Maui.Sample` (#226) for Android in Debug and in Release (ILLink and AOT on, arm64 and x86_64), and compiles its Mac Catalyst and iOS-simulator heads (`-t:Compile`: bundling needs Xcode 27, which the image lacks), all with `-warnaserror`. Then `tools/ApkAotCheck` checks that every AOT image in the Release APK holds the MVIDs of the assemblies the APK ships, the mismatch that crashed the Release app at startup in #366 (#368). The shell library itself builds in `build-test`; its tests are in `Broadside.Core.slnf`. |
| `uno / uno (webassembly + linux desktop)`, `uno / uno (desktop, <os>)` | ubuntu; macos, windows | Calls [`uno.yml`](#unoyml-the-uno-platform-sample-on-both-heads). |
| `winui` | Windows | Builds `src/Broadside.Viewer.WinUI` (#223), its sample `samples/Broadside.Viewer.WinUI.Sample` (unpackaged, Windows App SDK self-contained, `win-x64`) and `tests/Broadside.Viewer.WinUI.UITests`, all with `-warnaserror`, then runs the UI tests: FlaUI (UIA3) launches the sample on the pinned subset of sample documents and opens, scrolls (wheel, End, Home), zooms (toolbar, Ctrl+wheel), selects (a drag across a text node the automation peers place on screen, Ctrl+A, Copy), searches and toggles dark mode, and checks that the control's automation peers expose page 1's text in the viewer core's reading order. The library and the controller tests (`tests/Broadside.Viewer.WinUI.Tests`, in `Broadside.Core.slnf`) also build and run in `build-test` on every OS. |
| `avalonia` | ubuntu | The Avalonia viewer (#224): fetches (and caches) the corpora of the rendering gate's pinned pages (`pdfjs`, `pdf20examples`, `gwg-output-suite`), builds `tests/Broadside.Viewer.Avalonia.Tests` with `-warnaserror` and runs it headless (Avalonia.Headless with Skia drawing, no display server; at least 30 tests): each pinned page opens, its tiles reach the window's rendered frame as the rasterizer drew them, and it scrolls and zooms to sharp tiles again (`BROADSIDE_PINNED_REQUIRED` fails a missing pinned file), plus selection and copy, search with highlights and F3, touch pinch and double-tap, keys, links, a form-field editor, dark mode, worker-thread tiles and the automation peers' reading order. Then builds `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Avalonia.Sample` with `-warnaserror`. The library, tests and sample also build in `build-test` on every OS (full runs); the library is in `Broadside.Core.slnf`, the tests are not. |
| `ci` | ubuntu | Runs always, after every other job: fails if any of them failed or was cancelled, passes if each passed or was skipped by the plan. One check that stands for the whole run, for branch protection. |

A newer push to the same PR or branch cancels the older run. `DiffEngine_Disabled=true` keeps Verify from launching a diff tool.

### What a pull request skips

Issue #587. A pull request into the integration branch whose diff touches none of `global.json`, `nuget.config`, a solution or solution filter, `Directory.Solution.props`, `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/scripts/**`, `.github/actions/**`, `tests/Corpus/**` or `tests/Golden/**` (the corpus and golden images are read at run time by most test projects, which `dotnet-affected` cannot see) is narrowed to the projects `dotnet-affected` finds affected (project references, Central Package Management, `Directory.Build.props`/`.targets` and `.editorconfig` included). If the tool fails, the run is full. What a narrowed pull request leaves out, and where it still runs:

| Left out on a narrowed pull request | Why | Still runs |
|---|---|---|
| Any job none of whose projects (or listed paths) is affected: `aot-smoke` (`tests/Broadside.Rendering.AotSmoke`), `size-probes` (`bench/SizeProbes/*`, `tools/BenchGate`, `bench/size-probes.sh`, `bench/baselines/gate/sizes.json`), `verapdf` (`Broadside.Tests`, `Broadside.Fonts.Standard14.Tests`, `Broadside.Layout.Tests`, `CorpusFetcher`), `conformance-map` (the five checked packages, `ConformanceCheck`, `docs/conformance/**`, `site/articles/conformance.md`), `format` (any project it checks), `fuzz-build`/`fuzz-smoke` (`tests/Broadside.Fuzz`), `bench-dry` (the two benchmark projects), `blazor-wasm` (the Blazor sample or browser tests), `uno` (the Uno sample or UI tests), `maui` (the MAUI sample or `ApkAotCheck`), `winui` (the WinUI library, sample or UI tests), `avalonia` (the Avalonia sample or tests, `CorpusFetcher`, the pinned-page list) | The change cannot reach them | Every push to `main`, the nightly, pull requests into `main` |
| Unaffected projects in `build-test`; the whole `Broadside.Core.slnf` suite on Windows and macOS (only the platform tests and the render-hash test run there) | The core suite is managed code that behaves the same on every OS; the platform code is what differs | Same |
| `format` on unaffected projects | Formatting is per file | Same |
| The `Category=Exhaustive` sweeps (each runs as a fixed sample instead: every eighth corpus page as tiles, the first million of the twenty million CMYK colors, every sixteenth case of the two Unicode bidi test files) | Minutes of the Linux critical path for cases that rarely differ from the sample | Same, and in any `dotnet test` run without the filter |
| 45 of each fuzz target's 60 s, unless the target's code changed | A smoke regression net, not a fuzzer | Same, and `fuzz.yml` weekly |
| Packing (`packages` artifact) | Not every package is built | Same |
| `blazor-wasm` in the nightly | `blazor-wasm.yml` runs nightly on its own with every browser | `blazor-wasm.yml` nightly |

The plan job's summary lists the affected projects and what each job does. Allocation tests keep their assertions; `SkiaAllocationTests` warms up three replays instead of forty, because each case allocates nothing from its second replay on (traced per call in #587), and the measured calls after the warm-up still decide.

### NuGet cache

Issue #587. Before it, every pull request missed the cache and saved it again (147 s on Windows): a pull request's cache is scoped to that pull request, the integration branch had no run that saved one, the key hashed every `.csproj`, and macOS entries of 3.3 to 3.7 GB kept the repository at its 10 GB cache limit, so entries were evicted between runs. Measured on #588: a whole-solution restore is 3 GB on Linux too, and the Uno jobs saved 2.1 GB per operating system per pull request.

Now only Windows caches NuGet packages, where extracting them is what makes a cold restore slow (116 to 147 s). The key is `nuget-Windows-<hash of Directory.Packages.props, global.json and nuget.config>` (what decides the package versions), so editing a project keeps the exact key. `build-test` saves it, on its full runs only, right after restoring the whole solution, and only when it missed the exact key and either the run is not a pull request (pushes to `main` and the nightly save into `main`'s scope, which every pull request reads) or it restored nothing at all. A hit never saves again. `aot-smoke` and `render-determinism.yml` restore it on Windows without saving; `winui` keeps its own key (`nuget-winui-Windows-…`) under the same rule. Linux and macOS jobs restore from nuget.org: their restores are 3 GB and more (mobile and WebAssembly runtime packs), take 20 to 50 s cold, and caching them is what pushed the repository past its limit. `release.yml` keeps its own caches.

## `blazor-wasm.yml`: the Blazor WebAssembly sample in browsers

Called by `ci.yml` (input `browsers`), nightly at 03:47 UTC on the integration branch (`NIGHTLY_BRANCH`, `spec/33-broadside-v1`; GitHub runs schedules from `main`'s copy, so the nightly starts once this file is on `main`) and on the "Run workflow" button, both with `firefox webkit`.

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `blazor-wasm (chrome <browsers>)` | ubuntu | Installs `wasm-tools`, publishes `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Blazor.Sample` twice with `publish-static.sh` (trimmed and AOT-compiled; then `--no-aot --runtime-folder framework`, in its own obj/bin folders), and installs Playwright's `browsers`: `~/.cache/ms-playwright` is cached per Playwright version (read from `Directory.Packages.props`) and browser set, each install attempt is killed after 4 minutes and retried up to three times, and WebKit's system packages are installed with apt timeouts and retries (Firefox needs none: it runs on the libraries of the image's own Firefox). Then runs `tests/Broadside.Viewer.Blazor.BrowserTests` in the image's Chrome and those browsers, all required (`BROADSIDE_BROWSERS_REQUIRED`): a remote linearized file shows page 1 before the download completes, keyboard and screen-reader reading order, a phone profile with pinch-zoom, every demo feature at 390 px with touch in each browser (#338; the WebKit cases skip where WebKit is not installed), the non-AOT build booting from a host that refuses paths starting with `_`, no native binaries and the size budgets (issues #221, #338), and the browser kernel benchmark: every SIMD kernel's scalar and vector methods timed and compared in both the AOT and the interpreter build (#470; `kernel aot|interpreter` lines in the measurement log). Screenshots are uploaded as `blazor-demo-screenshots`. |

WebKit is not on every pull request because its system packages (about 120 MB of GStreamer and friends from the Ubuntu mirror) stalled the install past its 10-minute limit twice on #388, so the browser tests never ran (#389).

## `uno.yml`: the Uno Platform sample on both heads

Called by `ci.yml` (job `uno`); also runs from the "Run workflow" button.

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `uno (webassembly + linux desktop)` | ubuntu-24.04 | Installs `wasm-tools`, publishes `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Uno.Sample` for `net10.0-browserwasm` (Release) to `artifacts/uno-sample-wasm` and builds its `net10.0-desktop` head, both with `-warnaserror`; installs Playwright's WebKit and runs `tests/Broadside.Viewer.Uno.UITests` under `xvfb-run` with `BROADSIDE_UNO_REQUIRED=1`: Chrome and WebKit open, scroll (wheel), zoom (Ctrl+wheel, keys), select (mouse drag, double click) and search (Ctrl+F) in the browser head (#225), and the desktop head runs its automation script on X11. |
| `uno (desktop, <os>)` | macos-latest, windows-latest | Builds the desktop head and runs `DesktopHeadTests` (the automation script in a real window). |

## `bench-gate.yml`: allocations on every pull request that touches library, benchmark or corpus code; times on hot paths, `perf`, `main` and nightly

The benchmark regression gate (issues #139, #389; [`bench/baselines/gate/README.md`](../../bench/baselines/gate/README.md) has the rules, the thresholds, when times are compared and how to update the baseline). Runs when a pull request's diff touches `src/**`, `bench/**`, `tests/Broadside.TestSupport/**`, `tests/Corpus/**`, `tools/BenchGate/**`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json` or the workflow; nightly at 02:17 UTC on the integration branch (from `main`'s copy of the file); and on the "Run workflow" button, which takes a `base` (branch, tag or commit, default `main`) and `timing` (default true).

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | ubuntu-24.04 | Picks the head and base commits and decides whether times are compared: on a pull request into `main`, one labelled `perf` (read from the API, so a re-run sees a label added since), or one whose diff matches `HOT_PATHS` (lexer and parsing, content, filters and codecs, rendering and colour, fonts and text, SDK and package versions); nightly, against the branch's tip when the previous nightly ran (nothing merged since: nothing runs); by hand, per `timing`. Writes the decision and its reason to the job summary. The decision is `bench/gate-plan.sh`, tested by `bench/test-gate-plan.sh` (0 to 10 hot files, with and without `perf`, into `main` and the integration branch). |
| `allocations (<shard>)` | ubuntu-24.04, four shards | Picks this shard's methods with `tools/BenchGate shard` (`OpenAndWalk` split over all shards through `BROADSIDE_BENCH_PARTITION`) and runs `bench/run-gate.sh --measure allocations`: the head's allocation figures only (`Broadside.Benchmarks --gate-allocations`), no base build, no timing. About 10 minutes. Uploads `bench-gate-allocations-<shard>`. |
| `measure (<shard>)` | ubuntu-24.04, four shards, only when times are compared | Checks out the base commit in a second worktree and runs `bench/run-gate.sh --measure times`: the base commit's allocation figures (the stale-baseline notice), two interleaved BenchmarkDotNet rounds of both commits, and a rerun of any case the rounds find slower. 45 to 70 minutes. Uploads `bench-gate-shard-<shard>`. |
| `gate` | ubuntu-24.04 | Runs always, and fails first if `plan` failed or left an output empty (which would otherwise skip every measuring job silently). Downloads every shard's figures and reports and runs `tools/BenchGate compare` against `bench/baselines/gate/allocations.json`: one row per regression in the job summary and an `::error` annotation each, then fails if there is any, or if a shard failed. Uploads the baseline re-recorded from the run as `bench-gate-baseline`. Nightly, a failure opens the issue "Nightly benchmark gate failed on spec/33-broadside-v1" (label `area:ci`), or comments on it while it is open. |

A newer push to the same pull request cancels the older run. A run without times takes about 12 minutes; with times, about 70. The gate is not a required check: an intended slowdown is merged by the owner with the reason in the pull request.

## `bench-gate-perf.yml`: the `perf` label

On `pull_request_target` `labeled` with `perf` only (every other label skips its one job): finds the benchmark gate run of the pull request's head commit, cancels it if it is still running, and re-runs it (`gh run rerun`), so its `plan` job sees the label and times are compared. The gate itself does not trigger on labels, so that labelling a pull request for any other reason never starts, cancels or replaces a gate run. A pull request that changes nothing the gate watches has no run to re-run; use the gate's "Run workflow" button.

It is `pull_request_target` so that it also works for a fork's pull request, whose `pull_request` token is read-only. That is safe because the job is metadata-only: it checks out and runs nothing from the pull request, takes only the label name (in `if:`) and the head SHA (through an environment variable) from the event, and its token has `actions: write` and `pull-requests: read` only (the file's header comment has the reasoning; keep it that way). `pull_request_target` runs the base branch's copy of the file, so it works for pull requests into a branch once the file is on that branch.

## `render-determinism.yml`: the software rasterizer's bytes on every platform

The software rasterizer must draw the same bytes on every platform (issue #233). Runs on every pull request whose diff touches `src/Broadside/**`, `src/Broadside.Rendering/**`, the Standard 14 and CMap packages, `tests/Corpus/**`, the golden-image harness, `tests/Broadside.TestSupport/**`, `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Tests/**`, `global.json`, the shared props or the workflow; on pushes to `main`; and on the "Run workflow" button.

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `render (<leg>)` | `linux-x64` (ubuntu), `windows-x64` (windows), `macos-arm64` (macos), `linux-x64-no-intrinsics` (ubuntu, `DOTNET_EnableHWIntrinsic=0`) | Builds `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Tests` and runs the `RenderHash` trait with `BROADSIDE_RENDER_HASH_OUTPUT` set: every page of every hand-written corpus file at 72 and 150 DPI, rendered twice (the warm render must equal the cold one), hashed into `render-hashes.txt` with each render saved as a PNG. Uploads them as `render-hashes-<leg>`. |
| `compare` | ubuntu | Downloads the four runs and runs the `RenderHashComparison` trait with `BROADSIDE_RENDER_HASH_COMPARE` pointing at them: fails listing every render whose hash differs (or is missing) per runner, and uploads diff images (the first runner's render against each differing one, red where pixels differ) as `render-hash-differences`. |

## `corpus.yml`: weekly (Monday 04:17 UTC) and the "Run workflow" button

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `corpus-gates` | ubuntu | Fetches every non-manual corpus with `tools/CorpusFetcher`, builds in Release, and runs `tests/Broadside.Tests` with `--filter-trait "Category=Corpus"` and `BROADSIDE_CORPUS_DIR` set: the open-and-walk gate (#47), the veraPDF agreement, the real-world font, image and colour sweeps, and the content interpreter gate (#80, one class per corpus, with its allowlist and snapshots). Uploads `artifacts/corpus-gate/*.json` (per-file counts, diagnostics, time and allocation) as `corpus-gate`. Then runs `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Tests` with the same trait: the rendering gate (#138: every page of every file through the software rasterizer with every layer, no exception, no page over its processor-time budget, render diagnostics on well-formed files triaged in `render-diagnostics.allowlist.txt`, per-corpus snapshots) and the pinned subset (reviewed fingerprints, parallel renders equal to sequential ones). Uploads `artifacts/render-gate/` (per-file JSON and the pinned pages' PNGs; real-world renders are not committed, open decision 8) as `render-gate`. |

The corpus tests skip when `corpus/` is absent, which is why `ci.yml` cannot catch a regression in them; this workflow is where they run.

## `android.yml`: the Android backend on an emulator, weekly, on Android pull requests and the "Run workflow" button

Runs Mondays 05:17 UTC, on pull requests that touch `src/Broadside.Rendering.Android/**`, the display list (`src/Broadside/Rendering/**`, `src/Broadside/Graphics/**`), the Android test projects, the golden-image harness, `tests/Golden/**`, `tests/Corpus/**` or the workflow itself, and on the "Run workflow" button (spec #33 open decision 9: emulators are too slow and flaky for every PR).

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `emulator (API 35)` | ubuntu | Installs the `android` workload and the SDK packages it needs (`-t:InstallAndroidDependencies`), builds `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Android.Device` in Release for `android-x64` and the host project `tests/Broadside.Rendering.Android.Tests`, enables KVM, boots an x86_64 `google_apis` emulator with `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` (3 cores, 4 GB RAM, 576 MB heap; `-no-snapshot -no-audio -no-boot-anim -gpu swiftshader_indirect`, no cameras) and runs `.github/scripts/android-emulator-tests.sh`, which logs the runner's memory, CPUs and KVM, waits for the device to be attached and booted, and runs the host tests with `BROADSIDE_ANDROID_REQUIRED=1` (a missing device fails instead of skipping). The tests install the APK, then render the corpus files in batches of 8, one instrumentation run each (render through `AndroidCanvasBackend`, measure warm replays), pull each batch's gzip-compressed pixels over adb, 16 files per `adb pull`, and compare them with the golden images (issue #133). Robustness against the emulator's adb transport dropping to `device offline` (issue #344): the harness checks that the device is online and booted before every phase, retries install, clear and pull after `adb reconnect offline` (restarting the adb server on later attempts) with back-off, and reruns an instrumentation batch only when the transport cut it off before it reported a result code; an error the device reports (a failed install, a crashed or failing instrumentation) fails at once. When the transport stays down the tests fail with `adb transport lost`, and only then does the script reconnect and run the test step once more (the first attempt's TRX and adb log move to `attempt-1/`). Uploads the TRX, the harness's `android-adb.log` (every adb command with its exit code and time), the test console logs and, on failure, logcat as `android-test-results`, and on failure `tests/Golden/*.android.received.png` and `.diff.png` as `golden-images-android`. |

## `maui-android.yml`: the MAUI sample on an emulator, weekly, on MAUI sample pull requests and the "Run workflow" button

Runs Mondays 05:47 UTC, on pull requests that touch `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Maui.Sample/**`, the viewer shells it is built from (`src/Broadside.Viewer/**`, `src/Broadside.Viewer.Maui/**`, `src/Broadside.Rendering.Skia/**`), `tools/ApkAotCheck/**`, the Blazor demo's `DocumentCreator.cs`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json` or the workflow itself, and on the "Run workflow" button (spec #33 open decision 9, as for `android.yml`).

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `smoke (API 35)` | ubuntu | Installs the `maui-android` workload and the SDK packages it needs, builds the sample in Release for `android-x64` with `-warnaserror`, runs `tools/ApkAotCheck` on the APK, enables KVM, boots an x86_64 `google_apis` emulator (SwiftShader GPU) with `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` and runs `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Maui.Sample/smoke-android.sh`: install, start the smoke intent, and require `BROADSIDE_SMOKE_OK` in logcat (page 1 of the sample textbook chapter captured from the GPU surface) before a `BROADSIDE_SMOKE_FAILED`, a native abort or 300 s (#368). Then, on the same emulator, `uitest.sh android`: the intent extra `uitest` runs the sample's UI tests (`UiTests.cs`: every panel through its real controls by automation ID: search, annotate and save, view settings and dark mode, info, signatures, outline, thumbnails, create PDF/A + PDF/UA, and that the phone layout's bars fit the window) and requires `BROADSIDE_UITEST_OK` within 900 s (#358). |

## `maui-ui.yml`: the MAUI sample's UI tests on Mac Catalyst and the iOS simulator

Runs Mondays 06:17 UTC, on pull requests that touch the MAUI sample, `src/Broadside.Viewer/**`, `src/Broadside.Viewer.Maui/**`, `src/Broadside.Rendering.Skia/**`, the Blazor demo's `DocumentCreator.cs` (linked into the sample), the build props or the workflow, and on the "Run workflow" button (#358).

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ui (catalyst)`, `ui (ios)` | macOS | Selects the image's newest Xcode 27 (the workload's Apple packs need it to bundle an app; without one the job warns, says so in its summary and skips the rest, so the image lacking Xcode 27 does not block PRs), installs the `maui` workload, builds the sample in Debug for Mac Catalyst or the iOS simulator with `-warnaserror`, boots an iPhone simulator for `ios`, and runs `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Maui.Sample/uitest.sh catalyst|ios`: the app runs `UiTests.cs` (`BROADSIDE_UITEST=1`, `SIMCTL_CHILD_BROADSIDE_UITEST=1` on the simulator) and the job requires `BROADSIDE_UITEST_OK` before `BROADSIDE_UITEST_FAILED`, the app exiting or 900 s. |

## `fuzz.yml`: real fuzzing, weekly and on the "Run workflow" button

Every fuzz target under libFuzzer through SharpFuzz, one parallel job per target (issue #48; `tests/Broadside.Fuzz/README.md`, "Scheduled runs in CI").

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `targets` | ubuntu | Builds the harness and turns `--list` (or the `targets` input) into the matrix; checks the `minutes` input (default 80, at most 300 so every job stays under GitHub's 6-hour limit). |
| `fuzz (<target>)` | ubuntu | Builds the libfuzzer-dotnet driver from pinned, hash-checked source with clang; installs SharpFuzz.CommandLine 2.3.0; builds the harness in Release; fetches `pdf20examples` and `qpdf` with `tools/CorpusFetcher` (cached) as extra seeds; restores the target's libFuzzer corpus from the previous run (`actions/cache`, key `fuzz-corpus-<target>-<run id>`); runs `tests/Broadside.Fuzz/run-libfuzzer.sh` (which instruments a copy of `Broadside.dll`) for the given minutes on every core; saves the minimized corpus; uploads `stats.json` as `fuzz-stats-<target>`, and on a finding fails and uploads `fuzz-findings-<target>` (inputs, replays, worker logs). |
| `summary` | ubuntu | One table in the job summary: minutes, workers, CPU-hours, executions, corpus size and findings per target, and the cumulative fuzzing time of the run. |

Schedule: Sundays 03:17 UTC. A scheduled run fuzzes every registered target for 80 minutes: the 19 Phase 1 targets alone make 25.3 hours of wall-clock time (about 100 CPU-hours on the 4-core runners), and every target added later adds 80 minutes. Runs on one branch never overlap (they would race to save the same cache). From a terminal: `gh workflow run fuzz.yml --ref main -f minutes=30 -f targets="document save"`. A finding is fixed in a PR with a regression test next to the feature that rebuilds the input's mechanism (issue #48's are in `PredictorTests`/`FilterAllocationTests`, `CrossReferenceStreamTests`, `SaveTests` and `PageLabelTests`); replay the uploaded input with `--run` first.

## `docs.yml`: the documentation site

Runs on pull requests and pushes to `main` that touch `site/**`, `src/**`, `docs/**`, `.config/**`, `check-docs.sh`, `check-adr-refs.sh`, any top-level `*.md`, any `README*`, the issue and pull request templates, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json`, the Blazor demo (`samples/Broadside.Viewer.Blazor.Sample/**`, and `tests/Corpus/*.pdf` for its gallery), the guide samples (`samples/guides/**`) and `tools/DocSnippets/**`, or the workflow itself, and on the "Run workflow" button.

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `build` | ubuntu | Installs the `android` workload and the Android SDK packages it needs. Publishes the live demo (`samples/Broadside.Viewer.Blazor.Sample`) with `publish-static.sh` (the gallery reads the TraceMonkey paper from pdf.js's copy, which the repository does not carry; see the sample's README, "Documents and licences"): trimmed and compiled ahead of time outside pull requests, after installing the `wasm-tools` workload, and with `--no-aot` and no workload on pull requests, which takes about 6 minutes instead of about 10 (`ci.yml`'s `blazor-wasm` job publishes and tests the AOT build on every pull request). Then runs `./check-docs.sh --demo <folder>`: first runs `./check-adr-refs.sh`, which fails when a top-level Markdown file (except `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTEXT.md`), anything under `site/` or `docs/` (except the decision records themselves), any README, an issue or pull request template, or a `///` comment in `src/` cites or links an architecture decision record (see the script's header for the exact match); then checks that the sample code in the site's pages equals the regions of `samples/guides/` it includes (`dotnet run --project tools/DocSnippets`) and builds those samples (`samples/guides/run-samples.sh --build-only`), so a guide cannot show code that does not compile; then restores the local tools (`.config/dotnet-tools.json`, Lunet), builds `site/` with `lunet build` into `site/.lunet/build/www`, and fails on a Lunet error, a missing route (home, each article, `/api/`, the search index), a raw `.md` link, a package under `src/` without an API reference (a public type in its `PublicAPI` files with no page under `/api/`, or, for a package the job cannot build, not documented in `site/articles/api-coverage.md`), or an internal link or asset that does not resolve. `--demo` copies the published demo into `demo/` after the Lunet build and checks its routes, its runtime and its relative base href (which makes it work under `/Broadside/demo/`) with the rest. Lunet's `api.dotnet` module builds every package in Release, one target framework each (`net10.0`, `net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0` for Direct2D, `net10.0-android` for the Android backend), and turns their XML docs into `/api/`; `Broadside.Rendering.CoreGraphics` needs the Apple workloads, which do not install on Linux, so its API is written out in `site/articles/api-coverage.md`. On `main` it also uploads the output, demo included, as the Pages artifact. |
| `deploy` | ubuntu (`main` only) | `actions/deploy-pages` publishes the artifact to <https://michaelstonis.github.io/Broadside/> through the `github-pages` environment; the demo is at <https://michaelstonis.github.io/Broadside/demo/>. |

Pull requests only build and check. GitHub Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source (`build_type: workflow`), so nothing is pushed to a `gh-pages` branch, and Jekyll does not run, so the demo's `_framework/` and `_content/` folders are served as they are. The demo uses no WebAssembly threads, so it needs no cross-origin isolation headers (which Pages cannot send).

Locally, `./check-docs.sh` runs the same build and checks, without the demo (links into `demo/` are then left unchecked); `samples/Broadside.Viewer.Blazor.Sample/publish-static.sh --no-aot out/demo && ./check-docs.sh --demo out/demo` checks it too. To preview with live reload, `cd site && dotnet tool run lunet serve` (the dev environment drops the `/Broadside` base path).

## `perf-report.yml`: the "Run workflow" button

| Job | Runs on | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `report` | ubuntu-24.04, macos | The v1 performance comparison (#275): fetches the corpora of the pinned pages, installs PDFium and pdf.js (`tools/RenderDiff/acquire-references.sh`), and runs `bench/perf-report.sh`: Broadside, PDFium and pdf.js timed with one protocol on the rendering gate's pinned pages (open, text, render and first render at 72 and 150 DPI, the whole document at 150 DPI), peak memory per file, and, with the `browser` input, Broadside's WebAssembly build against pdf.js in the image's Chrome. Writes the run's report to the job summary and uploads the result folder as `perf-report-<os>`. |

Hosted runners are shared, so the numbers move between runs. To put a run in the published report, download the artifacts and run `bench/perf-report.sh --publish <folder>...` (`bench/baselines/v1/README.md`).

## `release.yml`: tags `v*` and the "Run workflow" button

1. `build-linux`: builds, tests and packs the core packages (`Broadside.Core.slnf`), including `Broadside.Rendering.Direct2D` (a single `net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0` target that builds anywhere through `EnableWindowsTargeting`). Packing runs package validation against the last published version (below). Then `tools/PackageCheck verify --online` checks every package it packed: dependencies on the per-package allowlist, symbol packages with matching portable PDBs, source paths mapped to `/_/`, every source document embedded or fetched through SourceLink at the release commit, licence metadata and files, README and icon ([`tools/PackageCheck/README.md`](../../tools/PackageCheck/README.md)).
2. `build-windows`: builds the Windows target of `Broadside.Viewer.Maui` (`net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0`, the `Platforms/Windows` handler) and uploads the assembly, PDB and XML docs as `viewer-maui-windows`. WinAppSDK's build runs `MakePri.exe`, so this target builds only on Windows, and the Apple targets only on macOS; neither runner can build the whole package (#381).
3. `build-macos` (after `build-windows`): installs the workloads, builds the full solution, tests `Broadside.Core.slnf` and the CoreGraphics backend, and packs it. It then downloads `viewer-maui-windows` into the Windows target's output folder and repacks `Broadside.Viewer.Maui` with `-p:BroadsideBuildWindowsShell=true` (restore, then `dotnet pack --no-build`), so the one package holds the `net10.0`, Android, iOS, Mac Catalyst and Windows assemblies, and fails if any of the five is missing (the listing goes to the job summary). It uploads only `Broadside.Rendering.CoreGraphics`, `Broadside.Rendering.Android` and `Broadside.Viewer.Maui`, so that every package comes from exactly one build, after running the same `tools/PackageCheck verify --online` on those three.
4. `reproducible`: `tools/PackageCheck/check-reproducible.sh` clones the commit into two differently named folders, packs `Broadside.Core.slnf` in each and fails unless every package file is byte-identical (the WinUI viewer is a reported exception: CsWinRT's source generator orders its output differently per build; see `tools/PackageCheck/README.md`).
5. `publish` (after the other three): merges the two sets into the `packages` artifact, with an SPDX 2.2 SBOM of every package (`broadside-<version>.spdx.json`, `tools/PackageCheck/generate-sbom.sh`, Microsoft's `sbom-tool` as a local dotnet tool). On a `v*` tag that is not a dry run it logs in to NuGet.org with trusted publishing, runs `dotnet nuget push --skip-duplicate`, and creates a GitHub release with generated notes and the packages and the SBOM attached (marked pre-release when the tag has a `-` suffix, e.g. `v0.1.0-preview.1`).

MinVer derives the package version from the tag (`v1.2.3` → `1.2.3`); a dispatch run on a branch produces `0.1.0-preview.0.<height>`.

### Release checklist

1. **Public API.** Every entry of each shipping package's `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` moves to its `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` at the v1 API freeze (#262) and, from then on, at every release tag, in the release pull request, so the next release's changes are the only unshipped entries. This covers every package under `src/`, the viewer packages (`Broadside.Viewer*`) included.
2. **Package validation baseline.** `PackageValidationBaselineVersion` in `src/Directory.Build.props` names the last version published to nuget.org (now `0.1.0-preview.10`); `dotnet pack` compares every package with that version and fails on a breaking change. In the release pull request, after the previous release is on nuget.org, raise it to that version. A breaking change between previews that is intended is recorded rather than reverted: pack with `-p:ApiCompatGenerateSuppressionFile=true`, which writes the package's `CompatibilitySuppressions.xml` next to its project, and commit that file with the change (from 1.0 a breaking change needs a major version instead). Delete the suppression files when the baseline moves past the version they excuse. A new package that has never been published sets `<PackageValidationBaselineVersion></PackageValidationBaselineVersion>` in its project file until its first release.
3. **Dry run** (below), then check its job summaries: every package listed, the package checks and the reproducible build green, `broadside-<version>.spdx.json` in the `packages` artifact.
4. **Tag** `v<version>` on the release commit and push it (a tag push publishes; only the owner pushes tags).

### Release dry run

Actions tab → **Release** → **Run workflow** → pick the branch or tag → leave **dry_run** checked → **Run workflow**. Or from a terminal:

```sh
gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f dry_run=true
gh run watch
```

The dry run builds, tests, packs and checks on all three runners, checks the build is reproducible and uploads the merged `packages` artifact with the SBOM, but pushes nothing and creates no release. It needs no secrets. Setting `dry_run` to false on a tag ref performs a real release; on a branch ref it still publishes nothing, because the push and release steps also require a `v*` tag.

### Release notes

The generated notes get a hand-written summary on top (`gh release edit <tag> --notes-file`). Every release from 1.0 on links the
[performance comparison](https://michaelstonis.github.io/Broadside/articles/performance/) (`site/articles/performance.md`), and,
when the release changes rendering, parsing or text speed, publishes a fresh run of it first (`bench/baselines/v1/README.md`).

### Trusted publishing (one-time setup by the owner)

The repository holds no NuGet API key. `NuGet/login` exchanges the job's GitHub OIDC token for a short-lived API key, which only works once nuget.org knows the workflow. Before the first real release:

1. Sign in to nuget.org as `stonis` (the nuget.org account; the workflow passes it as `user:`) → profile → **Trusted Publishing** → **Add**.
2. Repository owner `michaelstonis`, repository `Broadside`, workflow file `release.yml`, environment empty.
3. Push a tag: `git tag v0.1.0-preview.1 && git push origin v0.1.0-preview.1`.

Until that registration exists, only dry runs succeed; the login step of a real release fails with an authorization error and nothing is pushed.
